For a new small-business website in India, all three are legitimate choices. The main difference is price over time vs simplicity vs ecosystem.

Quick comparison
	Cloudflare Registrar	Namecheap	GoDaddy
Best for	Long-term ownership	Beginner-friendly domain management	All-in-one small business
.com first year	At-cost pricing	~$11.28 currently	~₹1,049 currently
.com renewal	At-cost / no markup	~$18.48	~₹1,499
Privacy	Included	Free for life	Included
DNS	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐
Ease for beginner	⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Upselling	Very little	Some	A lot
Hosting	No	Yes	Yes
Email	No bundled email focus	Available	Strong business-email ecosystem
Good for India	Yes	Yes	Yes

Current published pricing varies with taxes, promotions and exchange rates. Cloudflare explicitly says Registrar has no markup on domain names and no inflated renewal fees. 
Cloudflare
 Namecheap currently lists .com registration at $11.28 sale pricing and renewal at $18.48. 
Namecheap
 GoDaddy India currently advertises .com around ₹1,049 registration and ₹1,499 renewal, although promotional pricing can vary. 
GoDaddy
+1

1. Cloudflare Registrar — my pick

If you're reasonably comfortable with technology, I'd buy the domain here.

The biggest advantage is that Cloudflare isn't trying to make money by heavily marking up your domain renewal. It sells domains at cost. 
Cloudflare

It's also excellent if your website will eventually use:

Vercel

AWS

Google Cloud

Shopify

custom DNS

CDN/security

email services like Google Workspace

Downside: the interface is more infrastructure-oriented. If you've never touched DNS before, Namecheap/GoDaddy feels more beginner-friendly.

2. Namecheap — best balance

I'd choose Namecheap if you want something simple but don't want the GoDaddy ecosystem.

It's particularly nice for someone buying:

1–5 domains

.com, .ai, .in, etc.

domains for future projects

domains with privacy protection

Namecheap includes domain privacy for free on eligible domains. 
Namecheap

The downside is that its renewal pricing is higher than Cloudflare's at-cost model. For example, Namecheap currently lists .com renewal at $18.48. 
Namecheap

3. GoDaddy — easiest for a non-technical business owner

GoDaddy is probably the easiest if you want:

Domain → Website → Business email → Hosting → Everything in one account

It's very established in India and has an India-specific storefront/support ecosystem. 
GoDaddy

But I wouldn't choose it just for domain registration.

The classic GoDaddy issue is:

Cheap first year → considerably more expensive renewal → lots of add-ons.

GoDaddy itself notes that low introductory domain pricing doesn't necessarily mean the renewal rate will be the same. 
GoDaddy

What I'd choose for you

If you're buying a domain for a startup/business brand rather than just a hobby website:

🥇 Cloudflare

Best long-term choice

🥈 Namecheap

Best if you want the easiest domain-only experience

🥉 GoDaddy

Best if you want an all-in-one small-business package

And importantly, you don't need to buy your hosting from the same company as your domain registrar.

For example:

Cloudflare
→ yourcompany.com

Vercel
→ hosts website

Google Workspace
→ hello@yourcompany.com

That's actually the setup I'd recommend for a modern startup.

For a 50-person Indian company, Trip.com is better viewed as an OTA than a full managed TMC. Here’s the practical comparison:

Provider	Current price	Key exclusions / limits	Best for
Trip.com Flights	₹0 booking fee on eligible domestic flights; fare + airline charges apply 
Trip.com
	Not designed for commercial/business use under its India terms; no corporate policy/approval stack 
Trip.com
	Occasional employee bookings / price shopping
myBiz by MakeMyTrip	No published platform fee; corporate fares are quote/booking-based	Some benefits apply only to myBiz fares/hotels; cancellation rules vary by fare 
MakeMyTrip Biz
+1
	Indian SMEs needing GST invoices, policies and approvals
ITILITE	$10 (~₹830) per trip, or $7 with wallet; no subscription/support fee 
Itilite
	Airline/hotel penalties and fare differences remain payable; complex integrations may cost extra	Tech/startup teams wanting automation + policy control
FCM Travel	Custom quote; no public fixed fee	More implementation/account-management overhead	Companies wanting a full managed TMC, negotiated rates and 24/7 support 
FCM Travel
+1

For 50 employees: Trip.com is the least “managed”; myBiz is more India-native; ITILITE has the clearest published per-trip model; FCM is the most traditional managed-service approach.
